title: Coproduct inheritance and canonical restriction across indexing universes
statement:
Fix indexing universes $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, and let $P,Q$ be isomorphism-invariant properties of their objects. Write $\mathcal C_P,\mathcal D_Q$ for the full subcategories, and $i_P,i_Q$ for their inclusions. Assume that $P$ and $Q$ are closed under every existing ambient coproduct indexed by a type in $\mathcal V$: whenever all objects of such a family have the property and its coproduct exists, its coproduct object has the property. Coproducts mean colimits of discrete diagrams [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For a type $I$ in $\mathcal U$, $\operatorname{ULift}_{\mathcal V}I$ means a copy of $I$ in $\mathcal V$, with the canonical bijection to $I$.

Then $P$ and $Q$ are closed under every existing $I$-indexed ambient coproduct, with the same coprojections under reindexing by $I\simeq\operatorname{ULift}_{\mathcal V}I$. For every $I$-indexed diagram in either full subcategory whose ambient coproduct exists, that inclusion creates its coproduct and preserves and reflects its colimit cocones. In particular, if the ambient categories have all $\mathcal U$-indexed coproducts, so do the two full subcategories.

Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve the $\mathcal U$-indexed coproducts and suppose $P(C)$ implies $Q(FC)$. Its canonical restriction $\bar F:\mathcal C_P\to\mathcal D_Q$, sending an object to the same image $FC$ and a morphism to $F$ of that morphism, preserves all these coproducts. Under $i_Q\bar F=Fi_P$, its comparison map is the ambient comparison for $F$ using the inherited coprojections. If the ambient categories are triangulated and $P,Q$ are full replete triangulated subcategories [def-weil-triangulated-category, def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], and $F$ is exact, this canonical restriction is exact for the inherited triangulations. The empty index type is included. No generator-to-localizing-closure implication is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: Put $J=\operatorname{ULift}_{\mathcal V}I$, with inverse bijections $e:I\to J$ and $d:J\to I$. If $(L,(\iota_i))$ is an ambient coproduct of $(X_i)_{i\in I}$, it is also a coproduct of $(X_{d(j)})_{j\in J}$ with legs $\iota_{d(j)}$: given legs $a_j:X_{d(j)}\to M$, the unique required arrow is the arrow from $L$ with composites $a_{e(i)}$. The equations $de=1$ and $ed=1$ verify both factorization and uniqueness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Thus this particular $J$-indexed coproduct exists without assuming all $\mathcal V$-coproducts exist. The stated closure hypothesis applied to it gives $P(L)$ when all $P(X_i)$ hold. The identical calculation with $Q$ proves its smaller-universe closure, and retains exactly the stated coprojections.

proof.text: For an $I$-family $X_i$ in $\mathcal C_P$, let $(L,\iota_i)$ be any ambient coproduct. Step 1 gives $P(L)$, so $(L,P(L))$ and the same legs form a cocone in the full subcategory. For a cocone to $(M,P(M))$, its unique mediating arrow is the ambient mediating arrow: fullness allows it as a subcategory arrow, and equality of arrows is ambient equality. This proves the subcategory universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. It lifts each ambient colimit cocone on this diagram with its actual legs and vertex, hence proves creation in the usual sense of lifting and reflecting colimit cocones (up to the unique colimit isomorphism). The same construction applies to $\mathcal D_Q$.

proof.text:
An arbitrary cocone in $\mathcal C_P$ whose ambient image is colimiting is itself colimiting: restrict the ambient universal property to targets in $\mathcal C_P$ and use equality of the Hom sets. Conversely, if a subcategory cocone $(N,
u_i)$ is colimiting, compare it with the inherited cocone $(L,\iota_i)$ of step 2. The universal properties give arrows $a:L	o N$ and $b:N	o L$ with $a\iota_i=
u_i$ and $b
u_i=\iota_i$; uniqueness gives $ba=1$ and $ab=1$. For any ambient target $M$ and legs $t_i$, its required mediator from $N$ is $h b$, where $h:L	o M$ is the ambient mediator; uniqueness follows by precomposing with $a$. This proves preservation as well as reflection. Repeat for $Q$. If every ambient $I$-coproduct exists, step 2 supplies every subcategory $I$-coproduct.

proof.text: The condition $P(C)\Rightarrow Q(FC)$ defines $\bar F(C,P(C))=(FC,Q(FC))$ and $\bar F(f)=F(f)$; identities and composition follow from those of $F$. Hence $i_Q\bar F=Fi_P$ on objects and arrows. Start with any subcategory coproduct cocone on an $I$-family $(X_i)$ whose ambient coproduct exists, as in the statement (for instance when $\mathcal C$ has all $\mathcal U$-indexed coproducts). Its image under $i_P$ is colimiting by step 3, and its image under $F$ is colimiting by the assumed preservation. Its image under $\bar F$ is therefore colimiting by the reflection proved for $i_Q$ in step 3. This proves preservation of these coproducts for every $I$ in $\mathcal U$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: Choose the inherited source coproduct $(L,\iota_i)$ and target coproduct $(M,\kappa_i)$ of $(FX_i)$. The comparison for $\bar F$ is the unique arrow $c:M\to FL$ satisfying $c\kappa_i=F(\iota_i)$. Fullness makes this the very same arrow as the ambient comparison for $F$, whose defining equations are identical [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. It is an isomorphism because the cocone with vertex $FL$ is colimiting by step 4: the two universal-property arrows are inverse. All arguments in steps 1--5 allow $I=\varnothing$: the families of equations are empty and the coproduct universal property is exactly initiality, still giving the unique arrows and their uniqueness.

proof.text: Under the additional triangulated hypotheses, apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-restriction] with $\mathcal S=\mathcal C_P$ and $\mathcal S\prime=\mathcal D_Q$. Its hypothesis that $F(X)$ belongs to the target subcategory is precisely $P(X)\Rightarrow Q(FX)$; the full replete subcategories and inherited triangulations are assumed here. The resulting restriction is exactly the functor of step 4 on objects and arrows, with the restricted shift isomorphisms of $F$. It is exact for those inherited triangulations. This uses no assertion about generators or localizing closure.
